# Getting started {-}

All the labs of this workshop run in `RStudio`, in a Linux environment
providing `R`, `Bioconductor`, all the `R` packages, command-line tools and
datasets we will use. This environment is distributed as a **Docker image**,
built automatically from this book:

👉 [`ghcr.io/js2264/scrnaseqphysalia2026`](https://github.com/js2264/scRNAseq_Physalia_2026/pkgs/container/scrnaseqphysalia2026) 🐳

There are two ways to use it: in the cloud, on the Orchestra platform (this is
what we will do during the workshop), or on your own computer.

## During the workshop: the Orchestra platform

[Orchestra](https://orchestraplatform.org/) is an open-source platform,
supported by the Bioconductor community, which runs workshop environments in
the cloud. Each participant gets their own, isolated `RStudio` session, in
their web browser: there is nothing to install on your computer.

1. Open the Orchestra dashboard: **the link will be given by your instructors
   at the beginning of the workshop**.
2. Sign in with a Google account (any Google account works, either a personal
   Gmail address or an institutional account backed by Google).
3. Pick the **"Single-cell RNA-seq analysis with R/Bioconductor (Physalia 2026)"**
   workshop from the catalog and click on **Launch**. Starting the session can
   take a few minutes the first time (the status moves from `Pending` to
   `Starting` to `Ready`).
4. When it's `Ready`, click on **Open**: `RStudio` opens in a new tab, already
   logged in.

::: {.callout-warning icon='true'}
## Your session is temporary!

Every session has a time limit, shown as a countdown on its card in the
dashboard (you can extend it by clicking on `+1h`). **When a session expires
(or when you terminate it), everything in it is removed**, including the files
you created.

Download anything you want to keep (scripts, notebooks, results) before the end
of each day: in `RStudio`, tick the files in the `Files` pane, then click on
`More` > `Export...`.
:::

## After the workshop: on your own computer

If [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) is installed on your computer,
you can start exactly the same environment locally. In a terminal:

```{sh eval = FALSE, filename = "bash"}
docker run \
    --volume ~/scRNAseq_Physalia_2026:/home/rstudio/work \
    -e PASSWORD=physalia \
    -p 8787:8787 \
    ghcr.io/js2264/scrnaseqphysalia2026:devel
```

Then open [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787) in your web browser,
and log in with user `rstudio` and password `physalia`. The
`~/scRNAseq_Physalia_2026` folder of your computer is available in `RStudio`
as `~/work`: save your files there to keep them after the container stops.

::: {.callout-tip icon='true'}
## Memory requirements

Some labs load fairly large datasets in memory (the scATAC-seq lab needs
~12 GB): we recommend giving at least 16 GB of RAM to Docker (in
`Docker Desktop`: `Settings` > `Resources`).
:::

Alternatively, you can install all the packages used in this workshop in your
own `R` installation (`R >= 4.6` and a current version of `Bioconductor` are
required):

```{r eval = FALSE, filename = "R"}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("js2264/scRNAseq_Physalia_2026", dependencies = TRUE)
```

## RStudio

`RStudio` offers a graphical interface to facilitate the interaction between a
user and an underlying programming language (this is sometimes called IDE, or
integrated development environment). It can be very useful when a user is not
necessarily proficent with command line-based computing.

Don't forget, you can run a `bash` terminal from within RStudio! This may come
handy if you want to process some data with command-line tools (e.g. `seqkit`,
`samtools` or `cellranger`), for example. To do this, simply go to
`Tools` > `Terminal` > `New terminal`: a new `Terminal` tab opens next to the
`R` console. You should now be in your own home directory (`~`).

## Datasets

The labs download public datasets from GEO, ENA, 10x Genomics or
Bioconductor's `ExperimentHub`, using `BiocFileCache` (or the dedicated data
packages): a dataset is only downloaded the first time it is requested, then
read from a local cache. The datasets used in the `R` labs are already cached
in the Docker image, so they are immediately available in your workshop session.

The files that cannot be produced in a session (e.g. the outputs of
`cellranger`, in Lab 2) or that are specific to this workshop (e.g. the
datasets of the group projects) are available in the `~/Share/` folder of your
session (read-only: copy the files you want to modify to your home folder).
